vulnerability.name: Webmin Package Updates RCE
vulnerability.author: Thomas Shaw
vulnerability.description: This module installs a vulnerable version of Webmin, the Perl-based web system administration interface, which listens over HTTPS on port 10000. Webmin 1.996 and earlier are affected by CVE-2022-36446, an authenticated OS command injection in the Software Package Updates module (package-updates/update.cgi). The CGI concatenates the chosen package names (the request parameter u) into the shell command it runs to install updates without sanitisation, so an authenticated user who can reach that module can inject arbitrary operating-system commands. Because the Webmin miniserv process runs as root, exploitation yields code execution as root. The module creates a full-privilege Webmin administrator account (credentials in the webmin_username / webmin_password datastores) so the attack path is reachable. The Metasploit module exploit/linux/http/webmin_package_updates_rce automates authentication and injection. Note that CVE-2022-36446 was fixed in Webmin 1.997, so this module deliberately pins 1.996, the last vulnerable release.
vulnerability.hint: A Perl web administration panel on an unusual high port trusts the package names an authenticated user submits.
vulnerability.solution: Webmin 1.996 and earlier concatenate the selected package names into a shell command in the Software Package Updates module (CVE-2022-36446); authenticate and inject an OS command to gain code execution as root.
